title: Number lines and ordering
summary: Represent, compare and order positive and negative values on a number line.
objectives: Locate integers, fractions and decimals on a number line.
Order mixed positive and negative values accurately.

sections.title: Position determines order on a number line

blocks.text: Values increase from left to right on a horizontal number line. Therefore, the value farther left is smaller, even when both values are negative. For example, -8 is less than -3 because -8 lies farther left. Zero separates negative and positive values but is neither positive nor negative.

sections.title: Convert mixed representations to a common form

blocks.text: Fractions and decimals can be placed on the same number line after converting them to a common form. Use exact fractions when denominators are convenient, or decimals when place value makes the comparison clearer. Be particularly careful with negative values: among -0.6 and -0.65, the value -0.65 is smaller because it lies farther left.

sections.title: Absolute value measures distance from zero

blocks.text: The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero, so it is never negative. Opposite numbers have equal absolute value. The distance between two coordinates a and b is the absolute value of their difference.
Absolute value compares distance, while the original signs determine order.
